tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format, with no extra characters before or after the list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have generated the full move sequence and are ready to answer the problem.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing only a description or leaving the move list empty leads to a parsing failure.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move is not the topmost on its peg, first relocate the smaller disks that are on top of it to another peg, respecting the size rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before attempting to move any disk that is blocked by smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 4 sits on top of it results in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Consolidate all disks onto a single source peg before applying classic Hanoi recursion
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the initial configuration spreads disks across multiple pegs, first move all disks (preserving order) onto one peg so that the standard recursive Hanoi algorithm can be applied from that single source.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: If you prefer to solve the problem using the classic recursion and the initial state is not a single tower.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Applying the recursive Hanoi algorithm directly when disks are spread across pegs can reference non‑existent towers and fail.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, ensure that the destination peg is either empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the move violates the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg whose top is disk 4 places a larger disk on a smaller one and is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep answer concise and place move list at the very end
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer parser reads the last parseable list in the response; any text after the move list is ignored, and extra text before it can cause parsing errors or truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, output only the move list and nothing else after it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory sentences after the list can cause the parser to miss the intended moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is actually the topmost disk on its source peg; moving a disk that is buried under smaller disks is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 2 from a peg where disk 1 sits on top results in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary, move the nth (largest) disk to the target, then move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have a clean tower on a single source peg and need to transfer it to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to apply the recursion directly when disks are spread across pegs leads to illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the target peg already contains disks that are smaller than the disk you intend to move, first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere so that the larger disk can be placed safely.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the destination peg has a top disk that is smaller than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg where disk 4 is on top violates the size rule; you must move disk 4 away first.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model finishes without generating any moves, often because it assumes the puzzle is trivial or stops early.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always construct at least one legal move; if the initial state already matches the goal, output an empty list explicitly as [] but still provide it as the final answer.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of generation budget before finishing the full sequence, leaving the list cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Prefer concise solutions; if a long solution is unavoidable, break the reasoning into fewer tokens and ensure the move list is completed before the token limit is reached.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk to move without checking whether it is currently the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before emitting a move, verify that the chosen disk is the top element of its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to check the size of the destination peg's top disk, allowing a larger disk to be placed on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always validate the destination peg: it must be empty or have a larger top disk before moving a larger disk onto it.
